title: Zoho Voice pricing in 2026: What you need to know
summary: Compare Zoho Voice pricing across its free and paid business phone plans. See key features, usage fees, add-on costs, and a better option.
body_markdown:
Zoho has built a large ecosystem of business apps: email, project management, a CRM, accounting, and more. Zoho Voice is another offering in that lineup, giving businesses a VoIP phone system for calls and texts. Before you sign up, though, you should know exactly what you’ll be getting.


### Key takeaways


**


- Zoho Voice divides its plans into two categories: Business Phone and Enterprise Telephony. Business Phone uses group licenses that include multiple users. Enterprise Telephony uses a mix of per-user pricing and group pricing, depending on the plan.
- Solo is free for one user, and you can add more users for a fee. It doesn’t include a free phone number.
- Inbound calls and[SMS/MMS](https://www.quo.com/blog/sms-vs-mms/) are pay-as-you-go on Solo and Business Phone plans. Outgoing calls include free minutes based on the plan you choose. On Solo, you get those minutes when you add users.


Below, we’ll break down each plan, what you get, what costs extra, and an alternative to Zoho Voice.


##


**Zoho Voice business phone plans and pricing**


Zoho Voice has four Business Phone plans: Solo, Team, Office, and Corporate. Solo is free and comes with one user, with the option to add more for a fee. Team, Office, and Corporate each include one license and cover a set number of users.

### **Zoho Voice Solo plan**


**Pricing:** Free


**Users:** One per license, with the option to add more


**Best for:** Solo operators or very small teams


Zoho Voice’s Solo plan is designed for one-person use, with the option to add users as your needs grow. You need to add at least one user to get 250 outgoing minutes per month and access to SMS/MMS. It also unlocks features like voicemail drop, scheduled SMS/MMS, and call queues.


Here’s what you can use on Solo even without additional users:


- **Call recording.** Every plan comes with 1,000 minutes of free call recording storage.
- **Voicemail.** Solo includes voicemail, voicemail transcription, and the ability to download recordings.
- **Integrations.** As part of the Zoho ecosystem, Zoho Voice integrates natively with other Zoho apps like Zoho CRM, Zoho Desk, and Zoho Meeting.


### **Zoho Voice Team plan**


**Pricing:** $100 per license per month, billed annually


**Users:** Up to 10 users per license


**Best for:** Teams with more than five users


Zoho Voice’s Team plan covers up to 10 users per license. If your team is smaller, Solo with additional users may cost less — assuming you don’t need any of Team’s features. But if you can use most of Team’s 10 seats, the fixed $100 monthly price may make more sense.


Here are the notable features that come standard with the Team plan:


- **Free outbound minutes.** 1,000 free minutes per license each month.
- **Bring Your Own Carrier.** Keep using your current carrier while running calls through Zoho Voice. This requires Zoho Voice credits to set up and use.
- **Unlimited internal calls.** Make unlimited calls between team members.
- **Call transfers.** Transfer calls between team members.
- **Call disposition.** Categorize calls by type, reason, outcome, or status.
- **IM services.** Message customers through WhatsApp and Telegram.


### **Zoho Voice Office plan**


**Pricing:** $300 per license per month, billed annually


**Users:** Up to 30 users per license


**Best for:** Mid-sized teams


Zoho Voice’s Office plan is similar to Team but supports up to 30 users under one license. It also increases the free outgoing allowance from 1,000 to 2,000 minutes per month. Everything else stays the same, with the same features and add-ons as Team, and SMS remains pay-as-you-go.


### **Zoho Voice Corporate plan**


**Pricing:** $1,000 per license per month, billed annually


**Users:** Up to 100 users per license


**Best for:** Large teams with moderate call volume


Zoho Voice’s Corporate plan supports up to 100 users under one license. You get the same features and add-ons as Team and Office, but with 5,000 free outgoing minutes per month. Shared across your team, those minutes work out to less than three hours of free outbound calling per day.


### **Truly Unlimited plan**


**Pricing:** Contact sales


**Users:** Not listed


**Best for:** Businesses with high call volume


Zoho Voice also offers a Truly Unlimited plan for businesses with higher calling needs. However, Zoho doesn’t publish pricing or full plan details for this tier. You’ll need to talk to sales to find out what’s included and how much it costs.


### Zoho Voice Enterprise Telephony plans


**


Zoho Voice also has Enterprise Telephony plans for large businesses already heavily invested in the Zoho ecosystem. The higher tiers focus on call centers and include features like live call monitoring. Plus, every plan includes free incoming minutes.


- **Basic plan:** $34 per user per month. You get 1,000 free incoming minutes per user each month, plus unlimited outgoing calls to the US and Canada. Call listening, whispering, and barging are available as upgrades.
- **Standard plan:** $49 per license per month. This includes one admin account and 10 telephony agents. Telephony agents are users of other Zoho apps like Zoho CRM who can make calls through the ZDialer mobile app. They don’t have access to Zoho Voice, though. Each license includes 1,000 free incoming minutes and 250 free outgoing minutes per month.
- **Contact Center:** $74 per license per month. You get 2,500 free incoming minutes and 500 free outgoing minutes per license each month. Call listening, whispering, and barging come at no extra cost. Other features include the power dialer, queue performance metrics, and advanced noise cancellation.

##


**Zoho Voice’s true costs: Things you should know**


Zoho Voice’s pay-as-you-go rates and add-ons give you some flexibility to choose what you pay for. However, they also mean your final cost depends on how your team uses the service. Here are a few things to keep in mind.


### **Voice and text usage fees**


You need Zoho Voice credits for many calling and texting features. Service doesn’t get cut off when you run out of credits; you can keep calling as long as you buy more later on.


Here are the calling and SMS rates for the United States.


Calling and SMS rates Fees


SMS sending rates $0.009 per SMS


SMS receiving rates $0.007 per SMS


Receiving local calls $0.0085 per minute


Receiving toll-free calls $0.02 per minute


Outbound local and toll-free calls $0.0125 per minute


### **Understand how Zoho credits work**


Think of Zoho Voice credits like a prepaid card. You add money first, then use that balance for things like calls, texts, and certain add-ons.


Credits don’t come with your Zoho Voice license. You buy them separately at $1 per credit, on top of what you already pay for your license and any additional users. So if you’re on Solo and add four users, you’ll still need credits for your team to receive calls and send SMS. Any free outbound minutes included with your plan are separate and don’t come out of your credit balance.


When you need more credits, you can buy them from the subscription management page in your account. You can also have Zoho automatically add more credits when your balance reaches an amount you choose.


### **Solo plans need additional users**


Some Solo plan features only become available after you add at least one user. This includes SMS/MMS messaging and call transfer, along with features like business hours and call queues.


Adding a user doesn’t mean you get every upgraded feature for free, though. Add-ons like the power dialer and advanced noise cancellation still require you to spend credits. So you pay for the additional user first, then pay separately for any add-ons you need.


##


**5 Things to keep in mind before choosing Zoho Voice**


The price is only part of the decision. Here are a few other things to consider before you sign up.


### **1. Group texting isn’t available**


Zoho Voice gives your team shared contacts, but its texting is designed for one-on-one conversations. You can send and receive SMS with customers and track your team’s conversations. But you can’t create group text threads with multiple participants.


### **2. Track your spending carefully**


Many Zoho Voice features need credits, so you’ll need to keep an eye on your spending. Incoming calls are especially vulnerable. You can’t control how many calls your business receives, and a busy month may wipe out your credit balance.


Call recording, storage, and voicemail transcription can also use credits. The more your team uses these features, the bigger your budget needs to be.


### **3. Monthly vs annual pricing**


Zoho Voice costs more if you pay monthly instead of annually. The Solo plan stays free either way, but all the paid options cost more with monthly billing.


Here is how the pricing compares:


Annual pricing Monthly pricing


Additional users $19 per user per month $24 per user per month


Team plan $100 per license per month $120 per license per month


Office plan $300 per license per month $360 per license per month


Corporate plan $1,000 per license per month $1,200 per license per month


### **4. Trying out Zoho Voice is limited**


Zoho Voice offers a 15-day free trial, but it comes with a few restrictions. You can’t buy phone numbers or credits during the trial, although you can request two free credits to test outgoing call quality. If you want to test incoming calls or use other advanced features, you’ll need a paid plan.


### **5. Toll-free limitations**


Zoho Voice toll-free numbers can receive calls, but you can’t use them for outbound calling. They also cost more than local numbers when someone calls your business: 0.02 credits per minute for toll-free, versus 0.0085 credits per minute for local.

##


**Zoho Voice pricing: Pros and cons**


Zoho Voice can work well for small businesses with basic calling needs, especially if they have low usage and only need a few features.


As your team and call volume grow, though, its mix of licenses, usage charges, and add-ons can make it a less desirable option than a next-generation business phone system like Quo.


**Pros**


- **Flexible plans.** Zoho Voice offers several plans and add-ons. You can choose the features and pricing model that fit your team instead of paying for everything upfront.
-
- **Zoho integrations.** Zoho Voice connects natively with Zoho CRM, Desk, Recruit, and Bigin. This makes it a natural fit if your business already uses other Zoho apps.


**Cons**


- **Usage costs.** Zoho Voice charges extra for some features based on how much you use them. This includes incoming calls, SMS, call recording, and voicemail transcription. Your final bill will be hard to predict and budget.
- **Finding the right setup.** Figuring out the right Zoho Voice plan can be a headache. How many users do you have? Which add-ons will they use? How many minutes and messages do you expect to spend? Will you be adding more employees in the future? All those considerations and more will factor into the specific Zoho Voice plan you buy.
- **No group texting.** You can text customers one-on-one and share contacts across your team. However, Zoho Voice doesn’t offer group text threads with multiple participants. Quo supports group messaging with every plan.
- **No built-in AI voice agent.** Zoho Voice lets you route inbound calls to an external AI voice agent on every plan except Solo at $0.001 per minute. But you need to bring your own AI provider, such as ElevenLabs or Retell AI. Quo’s Sona comes ready to use on all plans.
